rationale: 306.7 states the planeswalker-redirection rule was removed, so a spell that deals damage only to players cannot hit planeswalkers instead.

508.1d states that if a creature can't attack unless a cost is paid, the player isn't required to pay it even if attacking would satisfy more requirements, so Amelia can decline to pay Ghostly Prison's cost.

116.2b and 702.37e each independently state turning a permanent face up is a special action, not an activated ability; 118.8 defines additional costs as applying only to a spell's mana cost or an ability's activation cost, so Exiled Doomsayer's increase to the morph cost isn't an additional cost that could be blocked from applying to a special action.
109.4a states a mana ability's controller is determined as though it were on the stack, so Moonring Island's mana ability is controlled by Anabella regardless of False Dawn.

116.1 defines special actions as not using the stack, and 113.3b defines activated abilities as things that go on the stack when activated; together these establish that Channel's mana-adding action is a special action rather than an activated ability Phyrexian Revoker's naming could stop.

729.1b states no effects or definitions created in the main game have meaning in a subgame except as defined by the effect creating it, so Nora's control of Abraham doesn't carry into the Shahrazad subgame.

609.4a states that if two effects allow doing the same thing 'as though' different conditions were true, both conditions can apply, so April's black mana can be spent as though it were any color and also as though it were colorless.

502.3 establishes untapping permanents as a turn-based action during the untap step; Undiscovered Paradise's return-to-hand trigger is tied to that turn-based action itself, not to whether it personally untaps.

712.9 and its example establish that a double-faced permanent copying another creature can still transform and remains a copy afterward; 701.27e states a 'transforms into' triggered ability checks the object's characteristics immediately after the transform occurs, which is what lets Instigator Gang's copied trigger fire.

303.4f requires an Aura entering the battlefield other than by resolving as a spell to attach to a legal object chosen by its controller; 115.10a establishes that being affected/chosen this way isn't targeting unless the word 'target' is used, so Deft Duelist's shroud is irrelevant.

608.1 states a spell or ability only resolves (and its effects begin) once players pass priority in succession on top of the stack, so Gliding Licid's activated ability hasn't produced any attach-effect yet, and no cost to end an effect that doesn't exist can be paid.

208.3 states a noncreature permanent has no power or toughness, so once Mirage Mirror stops copying Old Man of the Sea it has no power, which the control-changing effect's power condition treats as still satisfied.

400.7 states an object moving zones becomes a new object with no memory of its prior existence, so the graveyard object is a fresh 1/1 with no counters; 603.10a states leaves-the-battlefield triggers look back in time, so Paladin of Atonement's ability sees its toughness (4) immediately before it died.

723.1 establishes the 'control another player during their next turn' effect and its timing; 723.3 states only control of the player changes while objects stay with their normal controllers, so Mindslaver (still Charlotte's) generates its control effect under Charlotte, not Aubrey; 723.5 states the controller of a player makes that player's choices, which is how Aubrey was able to activate Mindslaver on Charlotte's behalf.

305.1 states playing a land puts it onto the battlefield the same as any other permanent entering, so Uphill Battle's 'enters tapped' replacement effect applies to Dryad Arbor even though it's played as a land.

614.17a states 'can't' effects must exist before the event they affect; since Solemnity enters simultaneously with (not before) Phylactery Lich, it can't stop Bronze Sable from getting the phylactery counter.

614.17a states 'can't' effects must exist before the event they affect; Suncleanser's protective effect on Prizefighter Construct already existed before Phylactery Lich and Hellkite Hatchling entered, so it successfully blocks the counter.

614.17a states 'can't' effects must exist before the event they affect; Tatterkite's own counter-prevention ability still existed immediately before Phylactery Lich entered (Humility entering simultaneously doesn't retroactively strip it in time), so no counter can be placed.
608.2c states a spell's controller follows its instructions in the order written, so Path to Exile removes Leonin Arbiter before the search-a-basic-land instruction is reached.

603.10a states leaves-the-battlefield triggered abilities look back in time, so Slimefoot's dies-trigger sees that it had lifelink immediately before it died even though it's dead by the time the trigger resolves.

708.2a states a face-down permanent has no characteristics beyond a vanilla 2/2, meaning face-down Blightsteel Colossus never had its own graveyard-replacement ability while on the battlefield, so nothing redirects it from the graveyard.

601.2h states a player pays the total cost (no more, no less); 702.51a defines convoke as tapping creatures rather than paying mana for the spell's total cost, so Ashley can't tap more creatures than the cost calls for.

608.2n states a spell is put into its owner's graveyard only as the final part of its resolution, so Beacon Bolt is still on the stack (not yet in the graveyard) while its own effect is being applied.

508.3a states an 'attacks' triggered ability won't trigger if a creature is put onto the battlefield attacking rather than declared as an attacker, matching Scourge of the Throne entering the battlefield already attacking via Kaalia.

701.44b states a permanent 'explores' only after the whole explore process is complete, by which point Volrath's Shapeshifter has already gained Nicanzil's text, so its new trigger condition is what's checked.

603.10 states objects are normally checked as they exist immediately after an event to see if it matched a trigger condition, so Blood Operative (now in the graveyard after the surveil event) is checked for its surveil-triggered ability at that time.

608.2c establishes that Merfolk Trickster's instructions (tap, then lose abilities) resolve in the order written, so Gran-Gran's ability triggers while it still has the ability; 603.3 states a triggered ability becomes an independent stack object with only the ability's own text once triggered, so it isn't undone by the source later losing that ability.

112.1 defines a spell as a card on the stack, so Soulfire Grand Master's lifelink-for-spells effect can't apply to Kozilek's Return while it stays in the graveyard and never becomes a spell; 702.88a states rebound's exile-and-recast trigger only applies 'if this spell was cast from your hand,' which didn't happen here.

603.3b lets Ariel, as the controller of the triggered abilities, choose the order they go on the stack; 603.5 states an optional-payment triggered ability's 'you may pay' choice is made as it resolves, not when it's put on the stack, letting Ariel time the untaps between Mentor of the Meek's payments.

603.12 states a reflexive triggered ability is checked based on the resolution of the spell or ability that created it, so Hypothesizzle's damage-dealing reflexive trigger checks Hypothesizzle's characteristics as it last existed on the stack, before Radiant Scrollwielder granted lifelink.

614.1 establishes the general behavior of replacement effects modifying an event; Gather Specimens' replacement effect causes Crafty Cutpurse to enter under Nylah's control, so the token Crafty Cutpurse's own ability creates is made under Nylah's control as well.

118.6 states an object with no mana cost represents an unpayable cost and that attempting to pay an unpayable cost is illegal, so Illusionary Mask can't be used to put the mana-cost-less Dryad Arbor face down onto the battlefield.

607.2a states that a printed exile ability and a second ability referring to 'cards exiled with this object' are linked, so Phyrexian Ingester's power/toughness-boosting ability sums up both Scarwood Goblins and Tor Giant, which were exiled by its own linked ability.

614.10 states a skip effect is a replacement effect whose choice must be made before the turn starts; 723.1 states a player-controlling effect applies during the entire turn but only starting at its beginning, so Norah still controls herself at the moment she must decide whether to skip the turn.

109.3 lists name among an object's characteristics generally, and nothing ties it to a specific zone the way power/toughness is tied to the battlefield, so Marble Diamond is still named 'Marble Diamond' on the bottom of the library and satisfies Predict.

616.1b requires that if any applicable replacement effect would modify under whose control an object enters the battlefield, one of those must be applied first, so Xantcha's own control-changing effect is applied before Essence of the Wild's copy effect can even consider it.

109.4 states only objects on the stack or battlefield have a controller, so a Dregscape Sliver card sitting in the graveyard isn't a Sliver creature 'Aspen controls,' and Pulmonic Sliver's granted ability (which only reaches Sliver creatures they control) can't apply to it there.
500.7 defines an extra turn as a turn added by an effect of a spell or ability, matching Medomai the Ageless's restriction against attacking during any turn that isn't a normal game turn.

608.2c establishes Austere Command's two destroy instructions resolve in the order written on the card; 701.19a states a regeneration shield protects a permanent only the next time it would be destroyed that turn, so the shield is used up on the first destroy instruction and can't also save Jhoira's Toolbox from the second.

603.2e states a 'becomes' trigger only fires at the moment the named state actually begins, not if that state already exists, so activating Spellskite's ability while it's already a target of Fiery Impulse doesn't make it 'become' a target again.

616.1 gives the affected object's controller (Amaya) the choice of which replacement effect to apply first; since neither Dralnu, Lich Lord's nor Furnace of Rath's effect falls into the earlier priority categories, 616.1e lets Amaya freely choose the order, determining whether 2 or 5 additional permanents are sacrificed.

707.2 states a copy acquires the copiable values of the original as they exist when the copy is made, so Colossapede's copy of Village Ironsmith doesn't update when Village Ironsmith later transforms; 712.9 states only permanents represented by double-faced cards or tokens can transform, and Colossapede (a copy of only Village Ironsmith's front face) isn't one, so it can't transform.

805.6a states that in a shared-team-turns game, each player on the active team may perform their draws in whatever order the team likes, so Arturo's team can have the partner draw first and let Arturo see that card before choosing for Underrealm Lich.

608.2b states a target is rechecked for legality as a spell or ability resolves, including whether its characteristics still meet the targeting requirement; once Siren Stormtamer leaves the battlefield as a sacrifice cost, Explosion no longer targets a permanent Nevaeh controls, so Siren Stormtamer's own ability has no legal target and doesn't resolve.

702.7c states that removing first strike from a creature after it has already dealt combat damage in the first combat damage step won't allow it to also deal damage in the second combat damage step, so turning Elvish Archers into a Frog afterward doesn't give it a second hit.

614.12a states that a choice required by a replacement effect modifying how a permanent enters the battlefield is made before that permanent enters, which for Show and Tell's simultaneous entry means both cards are known to both players before Asher must choose a creature type for Hall of Triumph.

601.2b states a player can't apply two alternative costs to a single spell, and Nourishing Shoal's exile-cards option is an alternative cost just like flashback, so having already cast it via flashback rules out also using the alternative cost.

701.3b states that an effect trying to attach an Equipment to the object it's already attached to does nothing, so re-equipping Fleetfeather Sandals onto Wandering Ones creates no new effect or timestamp; 613.7a ties a static ability's continuous effect timestamp to when it started, so Tightening Coils' later timestamp still wins in the layers, removing flying.

103.5 establishes that the starting player declares their mulligan decision first, followed by other players in turn order; 103.5b states an effect usable 'any time you could mulligan' is used at the point that player would make their own declaration, which for Albert comes before Nico has decided.

103.6 states that opening-hand actions like putting a permanent onto the battlefield from the opening hand happen only once the mulligan process is complete, so Ashley can't put Leyline of Punishment into play before finishing (and using) Serum Powder's mulligan-tied option.
